note: Meets the stated ICP on every criterion that was tested. He owns businesses in the cannabis industry, travels for deals, and keeps homes in two states — 'already successful, owns their own business' is met plainly. Income is inferred rather than probed: he never reacted to the $6,000 and the rep moved straight past it into a write-off pitch, so there is no direct evidence either way, but nothing suggests constraint. Health is the neglected corner of an otherwise ordered life by his own framing — "I work a lot, like a ton and I choose work over a lot of other things" — and it is explicitly good-to-great, which the rep tested and confirmed: "it doesn't sound like you're, oh, Harry, I'm 150 pounds overweight, my knees hurt" — "No." Not deconditioned in any sense: skis, mountain bikes, plays basketball three times a week, saunas and cold plunges. The finding here is not fit, it is the blind spot. The stated ICP has no clinical criterion, and this prospect passes all five while carrying post-surgical spinal history and current symptoms — exactly the exclusion that the ICP file's own observations say is missing and that decides whether the programme can safely serve someone.
